_comment: Hand-written prose biographies, merged into collaborator_bios.json by tools/merge_bios.py. Dates and affiliations come from Wikidata (tools/enrich_collaborators.py) and are not repeated here. Every line here is a claim we are prepared to defend; where we are unsure, the person is simply absent from this file and the site shows a blank.

bios.Brezis, Haim: French analyst working on nonlinear functional analysis and elliptic partial differential equations, and the author of a standard text on functional analysis. His fifteen papers with Bourgain, spread over 2000–2016, form the longest single thread in Bourgain's bibliography: Sobolev and BMO estimates, degree theory for maps into the circle, and the analysis behind the Ginzburg–Landau equation.
bios.Milman, Vitali: One of the founders of asymptotic geometric analysis, the study of convex bodies in high dimension where concentration of measure replaces intuition. His long collaboration with Bourgain runs from the mid-1980s Banach-space work through convex geometry and the slicing problem.
bios.Demeter, Ciprian: Harmonic analyst at Indiana University. With Bourgain he proved the ℓ² decoupling theorem for the paraboloid and the moment curve, which settled the main conjecture in Vinogradov's mean value theorem and reorganised a large part of Euclidean harmonic analysis around decoupling inequalities.
bios.Gamburd, Alexander: Works on spectral gaps, expander graphs and arithmetic combinatorics. The Bourgain–Gamburd expansion theorem for Cayley graphs of SL₂(p) turned a question about random walks in groups into one about additive combinatorics, and became the engine of the affine sieve.
bios.Konyagin, Sergei: Russian analyst and number theorist at the Steklov Institute and Moscow State University. His work with Bourgain concerns sum-product phenomena, exponential sums over subgroups, and the distribution of multiplicative subgroups in prime fields.
bios.Kontorovich, Alex: Number theorist at Rutgers working on thin groups, Apollonian circle packings and homogeneous dynamics. The joint papers with Bourgain develop the circle method in the thin-group setting and settle density questions for integral Apollonian packings.
bios.Lindenstrauss, Joram: Israeli mathematician, a central figure in the geometry of Banach spaces and, with Lior Tzafriri, the author of Classical Banach Spaces. He was among Bourgain's earliest and closest collaborators, from the mid-1980s work on almost Euclidean sections onward.
bios.Chang, Mei-Chu: Works in arithmetic combinatorics and additive number theory. With Bourgain she developed sum-product estimates in finite fields and residue rings, and their consequences for exponential sums.
bios.Sarnak, Peter: Number theorist at Princeton and the Institute for Advanced Study, known for work on automorphic forms, spectral theory and quantum chaos. With Bourgain he wrote on the affine sieve, Apollonian packings, and the Möbius function's disjointness from deterministic dynamics.
Number theorist at the University of New South Wales working on exponential sums, pseudorandomness and computational number theory; the joint papers concern exponential sums over subgroups and the distribution of arithmetic sequences.
bios.Rudnick, Zeév: Analytic number theorist at Tel Aviv University working on quantum chaos and the statistics of arithmetic sequences. The joint papers concern the spatial distribution of lattice points on spheres and related equidistribution problems.
bios.Mironescu, Petru: Analyst at Lyon working on Sobolev spaces and the calculus of variations. With Bourgain and Brezis he developed the theory of Sobolev maps into manifolds, lifting problems and the degree of such maps.
Lior Tzafriri, Israeli mathematician and, with Joram Lindenstrauss, the author of Classical Banach Spaces. The Bourgain–Tzafriri restricted invertibility theorem — that a matrix with unit-norm columns has a large well-conditioned column submatrix — is one of the most reused results in the subject and a precursor of the Kadison–Singer circle of problems.
Works on exponential sums and arithmetic combinatorics at UNAM Morelia; the joint papers concern sum-product estimates and character sums over subgroups of residue rings.
bios.Kalai, Gil: Combinatorialist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem working on polytopes, Boolean functions and the analysis of threshold phenomena. The joint work with Bourgain belongs to the Fourier analysis of Boolean functions and influence inequalities.
bios.Lindenstrauss, Elon: Works in ergodic theory and homogeneous dynamics, awarded the Fields Medal in 2010 for measure rigidity and its arithmetic applications. With Bourgain he wrote on entropy of quantum limits and on lattice points on spheres.
bios.Mirek, Mariusz: Analyst at Rutgers working on discrete harmonic analysis and pointwise ergodic theorems. The joint papers with Bourgain, Stein and Wróbel establish dimension-free and variational bounds for discrete averaging operators.
One of the defining figures of twentieth-century harmonic analysis, at Princeton for most of his career, and the teacher of a large part of the field. His late papers with Bourgain concern dimension-free estimates for maximal and averaging operators.
bios.Bombieri, Enrico: Analytic number theorist at the Institute for Advanced Study, awarded the Fields Medal in 1974 for the large sieve and the density theorem that bears his name. The joint work with Bourgain concerns exponential sums and the distribution of arithmetic sequences.
bios.Bulut, Aynur: Works on dispersive partial differential equations, in particular well-posedness and invariant measures for nonlinear wave and Schrödinger equations, which is also the subject of the joint papers.
Haskell Rosenthal, Banach space theorist at the University of Texas at Austin, known for the ℓ¹ dichotomy that bears his name. The joint papers belong to Bourgain's first period, on the structure of L¹ and 𝓛^p spaces.
bios.Wang, Wei-Min: Works on the spectral theory of quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators and on Hamiltonian partial differential equations; the joint papers concern Anderson localisation and quasi-periodic solutions of nonlinear equations.
bios.Wróbel, Błażej: Harmonic analyst at the University of Wrocław; the joint work with Bourgain, Mirek and Stein concerns dimension-free estimates for maximal operators and variational inequalities on ℤ^d.
bios.Berkson, Earl: Harmonic analyst at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, working on spectral decompositions of operators and transference methods, which is the subject of the joint papers.
bios.Ford, Kevin: Analytic number theorist at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign; the joint papers concern the multiplication table problem and the distribution of divisors and of integers with prescribed digital properties.
bios.Goldstein, Michael: Works at the University of Toronto on the spectral theory of quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators. With Bourgain he developed the multi-scale analysis behind Anderson localisation for one-dimensional quasi-periodic operators.
bios.Guth, Lawrence: Harmonic analyst and geometer at MIT, known for bringing the polynomial method into incidence geometry and restriction theory. With Bourgain he obtained the sharpest known bounds for the restriction conjecture by the polynomial partitioning method.
Svetlana Jitomirskaya, mathematical physicist at the University of California, Irvine and at Georgia Tech, known for solving the Ten Martini Problem on the spectrum of the almost Mathieu operator. The joint paper with Bourgain concerns absolutely continuous spectrum for quasi-periodic operators.
bios.Schlag, Wilhelm: Works at Yale on dispersive partial differential equations and on Anderson localisation for quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators; the joint papers belong to the latter subject.
bios.Kahn, Jeff: Combinatorialist at Rutgers working on probabilistic combinatorics, thresholds and the entropy method; the joint papers with Bourgain and others concern influences of variables on Boolean functions.
bios.Talagrand, Michel: French probabilist, awarded the Abel Prize in 2024, known for concentration of measure, generic chaining and the majorising measure theorem. The joint work with Bourgain belongs to the probabilistic geometry of Banach spaces and to influence inequalities.
bios.Alon, Noga: Combinatorialist at Princeton and Tel Aviv University working on extremal and probabilistic combinatorics and theoretical computer science; the joint work concerns Boolean functions and their Fourier spectrum.
bios.Ambrosio, Luigi: Analyst at the Scuola Normale Superiore in Pisa working on geometric measure theory, functions of bounded variation and optimal transport; the joint paper concerns fine properties of Sobolev and BV functions.
Works at the University of Missouri on frame theory and the geometry of Banach spaces, and on the Kadison–Singer problem, which is closely tied to Bourgain–Tzafriri restricted invertibility.
bios.Cochrane, Todd: Number theorist at Kansas State University working on exponential and character sums; the joint papers concern sums over sparse sets and over subgroups.
Freddy Delbaen, at ETH Zürich, known for the fundamental theorem of asset pricing in mathematical finance and, earlier, for work on vector measures and Banach space theory, which is where the joint papers sit.
bios.Dilworth, Stephen: Banach space theorist at the University of South Carolina, working on greedy approximation and the geometry of function spaces.
bios.Dirksen, Sjoerd: Works at Utrecht University on high-dimensional probability, compressed sensing and random matrices; the joint papers concern the restricted isometry property and dimension reduction.
bios.Dyatlov, Semyon: Works at MIT on microlocal analysis, quantum chaos and the fractal uncertainty principle; the joint papers with Bourgain establish the fractal uncertainty principle for Cantor-type sets and its spectral consequences.
bios.Figalli, Alessio: Analyst at ETH Zürich working on optimal transport, the calculus of variations and free boundary problems; awarded the Fields Medal in 2018.
bios.Fuchs, Elena: Number theorist at the University of California, Davis working on thin groups and Apollonian circle packings, the subject of the joint papers.
bios.Furman, Alex: Works at the University of Illinois at Chicago on ergodic theory, rigidity and group actions; the joint papers concern stationary measures and random walks on groups.
Alexey Glibichuk, working in Moscow on additive combinatorics in finite fields; the joint work concerns sums and products in prime fields.
Mikhail Gromov, one of the most influential geometers of the last half century, at the IHÉS and the Courant Institute, awarded the Abel Prize in 2009. The joint work with Bourgain belongs to the asymptotic geometry of normed spaces.
bios.Kahane, Jean-Pierre: French harmonic analyst, a central figure in the study of random series of functions and lacunary sets, and a long-serving member of the Académie des sciences.
Boris Kashin, at the Steklov Institute in Moscow, known for the Kashin decomposition of ℓ₁^n into two nearly Euclidean halves — a result at the heart of the geometry of high-dimensional spaces and, later, of compressed sensing.
bios.Klartag, Bo'az: Works at the Weizmann Institute on convex geometry and high-dimensional probability, in particular the central limit theorem for convex bodies and the slicing problem, which is the subject of the joint paper.
bios.Kutzarova, Denka: Banach space geometer at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences and the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
bios.Kristensen, Jan: Analyst at Oxford working on the calculus of variations, quasiconvexity and regularity theory.
bios.Mozes, Shahar: Works at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem on ergodic theory, lattices in Lie groups and group actions on buildings.
bios.Naor, Assaf: Works at Princeton on metric geometry, the theory of metric embeddings and their connections with theoretical computer science.
bios.Nelson, Jelani: Theoretical computer scientist at the University of California, Berkeley working on sketching, streaming algorithms and dimension reduction; the joint work concerns the restricted isometry property of structured random matrices.
bios.Nguyen, Hoai-Minh: Analyst at Sorbonne Université working on partial differential equations, in particular Sobolev space characterisations and the mathematics of metamaterials and cloaking.
Alain Pajor, convex geometer at Université Gustave Eiffel, working on the asymptotic theory of finite-dimensional normed spaces and on random matrices.
bios.Pełczynski, Aleksander: Polish mathematician, one of the founders of the modern geometry of Banach spaces, at the Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences.
bios.Pinner, Christopher: Number theorist at Kansas State University working on exponential sums and Waring-type problems in finite fields.
bios.Pisier, Gilles: French mathematician at Sorbonne Université and Texas A&M, a central figure in the geometry of Banach spaces, probability in Banach spaces and operator space theory.
Stanisław Szarek, at Case Western Reserve University and Sorbonne Université, working on the asymptotic geometry of convex bodies, random matrices and quantum information theory.
bios.Watt, Nigel: Analytic number theorist working on exponential sums and the divisor and circle problems.
Przemysław Wojtaszczyk, at the Polish Academy of Sciences and the University of Warsaw, working on approximation theory, greedy algorithms and Banach spaces of analytic functions.
bios.Yehudayoff, Amir: Theoretical computer scientist at the Technion and the University of Copenhagen, working on complexity theory, communication complexity and the interface with combinatorics.
Aleksei Aleksandrov, at the Steklov Institute in St Petersburg, working on complex and harmonic analysis, Hardy spaces and singular integrals.
Vitaly Bergelson, at Ohio State University, one of the founders of ergodic Ramsey theory; the polynomial Szemerédi theorem of Bergelson and Leibman is a landmark of the subject.
bios.Bethuel, Fabrice: Analyst at Sorbonne Université working on the calculus of variations and on the Ginzburg–Landau equation, on which he wrote a standard monograph with Brezis and Hélein.
bios.Blomer, Valentin: Analytic number theorist at the University of Bonn working on automorphic forms, L-functions and subconvexity.
Michael Boshernitzan, at Rice University, worked on ergodic theory, interval exchange transformations and Diophantine approximation.
bios.Burq, Nicolas: Analyst at Université Paris-Saclay working on the propagation of waves, control theory for dispersive equations and random initial data.
bios.Clozel, Laurent: French number theorist at Université Paris-Saclay working on automorphic forms and the Langlands programme; the joint work concerns spectral gaps for group actions on spheres.
James Colliander, at the University of British Columbia, works on nonlinear dispersive partial differential equations and was part of the I-team that developed the I-method for low-regularity well-posedness.
bios.Connes, Alain: French mathematician at the IHÉS and the Collège de France, the founder of noncommutative geometry, awarded the Fields Medal in 1982.
bios.Diestel, Joe: Banach space theorist at Kent State University, known for his books on vector measures and on sequences and series in Banach spaces.
bios.Dvir, Zeev: Theoretical computer scientist at Princeton, known for the polynomial-method proof of the finite field Kakeya conjecture.
Tadeusz Figiel, at the Polish Academy of Sciences in Gdańsk, working on the geometry of Banach spaces; the Figiel–Lindenstrauss–Milman theorem on almost Euclidean sections is one of the foundations of the local theory.
British mathematician at the University of Essex, the author of a five-volume treatise on measure theory; the Bourgain–Fremlin–Talagrand theorem on pointwise compact sets of Baire class one functions is a joint landmark.
bios.Friedgut, Ehud: Combinatorialist at the Weizmann Institute working on the Fourier analysis of Boolean functions, sharp thresholds and extremal set theory.
bios.Ghoussoub, Nassif: Analyst at the University of British Columbia working on nonlinear analysis, variational methods and Banach space geometry.
Alastair Gillespie, at the University of Edinburgh, worked on operator theory, spectral decompositions and transference in harmonic analysis.
bios.Golse, François: Analyst at the École polytechnique working on kinetic theory, the Boltzmann equation and hydrodynamic limits.
F. Alberto Grünbaum, at the University of California, Berkeley, works on integrable systems, orthogonal polynomials and the mathematics of tomography.
Victor Havin, at St Petersburg State University, worked on complex and harmonic analysis, uncertainty principles and the theory of Hardy spaces.
Analyst at Yale working on harmonic analysis, quasiconformal mappings and the geometry of sets, and known for the travelling salesman theorem that bears his name.
bios.Kachkovskiy, Ilya: Works at Michigan State University on the spectral theory of quasi-periodic and random Schrödinger operators.
bios.Kaloshin, Vadim: Works at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria on dynamical systems, Arnold diffusion and inverse spectral problems for billiards.
Nigel Kalton, at the University of Missouri, was one of the most prolific Banach space theorists of his generation, working on quasi-Banach spaces, interpolation and nonlinear geometry.
bios.Katznelson, Yitzhak: Harmonic analyst at Stanford and the Hebrew University, the author of a standard introduction to harmonic analysis, with later work in ergodic theory and combinatorics.
Analyst at the University of Chicago working on harmonic analysis, elliptic boundary value problems and dispersive equations, and known for the concentration-compactness/rigidity method developed with Frank Merle.
bios.Kesten, Harry: Probabilist at Cornell, a founding figure of percolation theory and of random walks on groups.
bios.Klainerman, Sergiu: Analyst at Princeton working on nonlinear hyperbolic equations and general relativity, and known for the null condition and the vector field method.
bios.Klein, Abel: Mathematical physicist at the University of California, Irvine, working on random Schrödinger operators, Anderson localisation and multi-scale analysis.
bios.Kozma, Gady: Probabilist at the Weizmann Institute working on random walks, percolation and harmonic analysis.
bios.Larsen, Michael: Works at Indiana University on group theory, representation theory and arithmetic geometry; the joint work concerns growth and expansion in finite simple groups.
bios.Lewko, Mark: Works on harmonic analysis and additive combinatorics, in particular restriction estimates and their arithmetic applications.
bios.Linial, Nathan: Combinatorialist and theoretical computer scientist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, known for work on the influence of variables on Boolean functions and on metric embeddings.
bios.Machedon, Matei: Analyst at the University of Maryland working on nonlinear wave equations, null forms and the derivation of effective equations from many-body dynamics.
bios.Magee, Michael: Works at Durham University on random matrices, random surfaces and spectral gaps for group actions.
Boris Makarov, at St Petersburg State University, worked on real analysis, measure theory and function spaces.
Mathieu Meyer, convex geometer at Université Gustave Eiffel, working on volume inequalities and the Mahler conjecture.
bios.Michel, Philippe: Analytic number theorist at the EPFL working on automorphic forms, L-functions and subconvexity, and on equidistribution problems.
Alexander Olevskii, at Tel Aviv University, works on harmonic analysis, Fourier series, sampling and interpolation, and uniqueness problems.
bios.Orlandi, Giandomenico: Analyst at the University of Verona working on the calculus of variations, geometric measure theory and Ginzburg–Landau vortices.
bios.Pavlović, Nataša: Analyst at the University of Texas at Austin working on nonlinear dispersive equations, fluid equations and many-body quantum dynamics.
bios.Pomerance, Carl: Number theorist at Dartmouth College working on computational and elementary number theory, primality testing and factoring.
bios.Preiss, David: Analyst at the University of Warwick working on geometric measure theory and differentiability, and known for his theorem on measures with prescribed densities.
bios.Radziwiłł, Maksym: Analytic number theorist at the University of Texas at Austin working on multiplicative functions, moments of L-functions and the Chowla and Erdős–Kac circles of problems.
bios.Reshetikhin, Nicolai: Mathematical physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and Tsinghua, working on quantum groups, integrable systems and invariants of three-manifolds.
Gideon Schechtman, at the Weizmann Institute, works on the geometry of Banach spaces, concentration of measure and metric embeddings.
Yakov Sinai, at Princeton and the Landau Institute, one of the founders of modern dynamical systems and statistical mechanics; awarded the Abel Prize in 2014.
Harmonic analyst at Johns Hopkins University, known for his eigenfunction estimates on compact manifolds and for work on Fourier integral operators and nonlinear wave equations.
bios.Szankowski, Andrzej: At the Hebrew University of Jerusalem; worked on the geometry of Banach spaces and the approximation property, showing that B(H) fails it.
At the University of California, Los Angeles, awarded the Fields Medal in 2006; he works across harmonic analysis, additive combinatorics, partial differential equations and number theory. The Bourgain–Katz–Tao sum-product theorem in finite fields is a joint result with wide consequences.
Nicole Tomczak-Jaegermann, at the University of Alberta, worked on the asymptotic geometry of finite-dimensional normed spaces and on random matrices.
Works at the University of Cambridge on random walks on groups, expansion and Bernoulli convolutions.
bios.Venkatesh, Akshay: Number theorist at the Institute for Advanced Study, awarded the Fields Medal in 2018 for work connecting analytic number theory, homogeneous dynamics and topology.
Anatoly Vershik, at the Steklov Institute in St Petersburg, works on representation theory, ergodic theory and the asymptotic combinatorics of symmetric groups.
bios.Voiculescu, Dan-Virgil: At the University of California, Berkeley, the founder of free probability theory and of free entropy.
Probabilist and combinatorialist at Yale working on random matrices, additive combinatorics and probabilistic combinatorics.
bios.Wennberg, Bernt: Analyst at Chalmers University of Technology working on kinetic theory and the Boltzmann equation.
Jon Wilkening, at the University of California, Berkeley, works on computational mathematics, free-surface flows and numerical methods for nonlinear waves.
bios.Wojciechowski, Michał: At the Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences; works on harmonic analysis, Sobolev spaces and function spaces on the torus.
Thomas Wolff worked at Caltech on harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory; his work on the Kakeya problem, local smoothing and the corona theorem reshaped the subject, and he died in 2000 at the age of 46.
bios.Wood, Philip Matchett: Works at Harvard on random matrices, random graphs and probabilistic combinatorics.
bios.Wright, James: Harmonic analyst at the University of Edinburgh working on oscillatory integrals, singular Radon transforms and their arithmetic analogues.
bios.Zhang, Gaoyong: Convex geometer at NYU Tandon working on the Brunn–Minkowski theory and affine isoperimetric inequalities.
Tamar Ziegler, at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, works on ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis and their applications to patterns in the primes.
bios.Zworski, Maciej: Analyst at the University of California, Berkeley working on microlocal analysis, scattering theory, resonances and quantum chaos.
bios.Kemp, Dominique: Works on decoupling inequalities and restriction theory in harmonic analysis.
bios.Guo, Shaoming: Harmonic analyst at the University of Wisconsin–Madison working on decoupling, oscillatory integrals and their number-theoretic applications.
bios.Asmar, Nakhlé: Harmonic analyst at the University of Missouri working on transference methods, conjugate functions and analysis on groups.
bios.Haslinger, Friedrich: At the University of Vienna; works on several complex variables and the ∂̄-Neumann problem.
bios.Benyamini, Yoav: At the Technion; worked on Banach space geometry and the nonlinear theory of Banach spaces, on which he wrote a monograph with Joram Lindenstrauss.
bios.Reinov, Oleg: At St Petersburg State University; works on operator ideals, approximation properties and tensor products of Banach spaces.
Evgenii Semenov, at Voronezh State University, works on the theory of rearrangement-invariant function spaces and interpolation.
Spiros Argyros, at the National Technical University of Athens, constructs Banach spaces with extreme properties; the Argyros–Haydon space solved the scalar-plus-compact problem.
William J. Davis, at Ohio State University, worked on the geometry of Banach spaces; the Davis–Figiel–Johnson–Pełczyński factorisation of weakly compact operators is a standard tool.
bios.Aizenberg, Lev: Worked at Bar-Ilan University on several complex variables, integral representations and analytic continuation.
Works at Fudan University on the analysis of the Navier–Stokes equations and on fine properties of Sobolev functions.
Vyacheslav Zakharyuta, at Sabancı University, works on complex analysis, pluripotential theory and spaces of analytic functions.
bios.Li, Dong: Analyst working on nonlinear dispersive and fluid partial differential equations.
bios.Paulhus, Jennifer: Number theorist working on Jacobians of curves and their decompositions.
bios.Yao, Xiaohua: Analyst at Central China Normal University working on dispersive estimates and spectral theory for Schrödinger operators.
Nets Katz, harmonic analyst and combinatorialist, at Rice University and previously Caltech. The Bourgain–Katz–Tao sum-product theorem in finite fields is joint work with him — not with Nicholas Katz, whom automatic name matching tends to substitute.
